the user-centered design process of the interface of the future interlocking system is characterized by an innovative approach, which is based on the methodological framework of usability engineering, and the results of the design are a prototype of a decluttered user interface for the control panel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how a human-centered design of rail traffic controllers' work environment can be achieved.
the development of a user-centred interface for rail traffic controllers, based on the principles of human-centred design.
the question how the future workplace of rail traffic controllers should look like and how it should be designed in order to support the controller in his work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the usability experts were able to generate a design that was based on the feedback of rail traffic controllers and was in accordance with usability principles.
a future rail traffic controller's workplace can be designed to be user-centred and thus, more efficient and safe.
the design of future workplaces in rail traffic control rooms should be based on a user-centered approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human-machine interface of the future rail traffic controller’s workplace should be designed to be user-centered.
the user-centred design process has led to a design concept which has a high potential to support rail traffic controllers in their work.

the user interface design of the future interlocking system should focus on the following aspects: a) the central display / control should be decluttered and reduced to the essential functions, b) the central control should be located on a single monitor and c) the user interface should be adapted to the user's needs and expectations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human-machine interface of a railway system should be designed in a user-centred manner, with a focus on the human as the key user in the rail traffic controller's workplace.
user-centred design is a powerful tool for the development of innovative human-machine interfaces in the railway domain.
user-centred design is an important tool for the development of future rail human factors.
